sources.title: The Norwegian model of lactate threshold training and lactate controlled approach to training
sources.scope_note: Bakken explicitly describes this as empirical reflection, not a scientific article. It concerns elite distance running and lactate-guided training, not an individualized triathlon prescription.

passages.text: The author states that the article is not scientific and presents thoughts, reflections, and experience from an empirical perspective.

passages.locator: Finding the sweet spot training zone
passages.text: Bakken describes optimizing training by measuring, testing, and adjusting workouts rather than applying a fixed threshold number universally.

passages.locator: Finding the sweet spot training zone
passages.text: He warns that threshold lactate is individual and says better athletes eventually need accurate laboratory or field measurement.

passages.locator: Finding the sweet spot training zone
passages.text: His experience placed longer intervals mostly just below threshold, with shorter intervals nearer threshold.

sources.title: Double Threshold Training in Depth: What It Is, Why It Works, and How to Use It
sources.scope_note: The practical prescriptions reflect Bakken's elite-running experience. Research discussion within the article is not treated as proof of a specific dose for this athlete.

passages.locator: What Double Threshold Training Actually Is
passages.text: Double threshold uses two controlled threshold sessions in one day, separated by hours, to accumulate work without one oversized session.
Bakken notes that frequent accumulated load carried risk and describes respecting the following recovery day.

sources.title: Understanding Your 80/20 Triathlon Plan
sources.scope_note: Official public 80/20 Endurance web guidance. This is not imported book content and must not be cited as the book.

passages.text: A workout segment may be performed anywhere within its prescribed zone; always using the upper end is not necessarily better.
The guidance prefers consistent moderate and high intervals over pushing each repeat progressively harder.
The swim examples prescribe work by distance and passive recovery by seconds.

passages.locator: The Importance of Listening to Your Body
passages.text: The plan is conditional on circumstances; athlete feedback and alarming soreness can justify changing or stopping a session.

sources.title: Intensity Guidelines for 80/20 Triathlon
sources.scope_note: Official public 80/20 Endurance web guidance. Its seven-zone scale remains distinct from Norwegian lactate terminology.

passages.text: The article distinguishes power as output, pace as outcome, and heart rate as an indicator affected by conditions.
The 80/20 zones are derived from a tested personal threshold rather than from a generic athlete value.
Swim threshold pace is estimated from a 400/200 critical-velocity test or a documented alternative test.

sources.title: How to Set a Good Race Time Goal – A Breakthrough Strategy
sources.scope_note: Public running-focused guidance; triathlon targets require discipline-specific performance data and course/context adjustments.

passages.locator: How to Set a Good Race Time Goal
passages.text: Intensity zones are too broad on their own to establish a precise race-time target.

passages.locator: Think in terms of incremental improvements
passages.text: Race goals should be informed by comparable past performances, current training, key workouts, and preparatory races.
Fitness, course profile, and expected conditions should all be considered when setting a target.

sources.title: Which Training Intensity Distribution Intervention will Produce the Greatest Improvements in Maximal Oxygen Uptake and Time-Trial Performance in Endurance Athletes?
sources.scope_note: Thirteen studies, 348 recreational and competitive endurance athletes. Outcomes and relative benefits differed by performance level; this does not prescribe an individual's exact weekly split.

passages.text: No training-intensity distribution was universally superior; responses differed between recreational and competitive athletes.

sources.title: Monitoring Athlete Training Loads: Consensus Statement
sources.scope_note: Multidisciplinary consensus framework for athlete-load monitoring; it supports using monitoring in decisions but does not validate a single readiness score or exact adjustment.

passages.text: The consensus describes multidisciplinary monitoring of internal and external load to inform performance and health decisions.
